title: "He Ascended into Heaven and is Seated at the Right Hand of the Father"

breadcrumb.label: Article 6
breadcrumb.title: "He Ascended into Heaven and is Seated at the Right Hand of the Father"

blocks.html: "So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God."<sup class="fn" data-fn="531">531</sup> Christ's body was glorified at the moment of his Resurrection, as proved by the new and supernatural properties it subsequently and permanently enjoys.<sup class="fn" data-fn="532">532</sup> But during the forty days when he eats and drinks familiarly with his disciples and teaches them about the kingdom, his glory remains veiled under the appearance of ordinary humanity.<sup class="fn" data-fn="533">533</sup> Jesus' final apparition ends with the irreversible entry of his humanity into divine glory, symbolized by the cloud and by heaven, where he is seated from that time forward at God's right hand.<sup class="fn" data-fn="534">534</sup> Only in a wholly exceptional and unique way would Jesus show himself to Paul "as to one untimely born", in a last apparition that established him as an apostle.<sup class="fn" data-fn="535">535</sup>

The veiled character of the glory of the Risen One during this time is intimated in his mysterious words to Mary Magdalene: "I have not yet ascended to the Father; but go to my brethren and say to them, I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."<sup class="fn" data-fn="536">536</sup> This indicates a difference in manifestation between the glory of the risen Christ and that of the Christ exalted to the Father's right hand, a transition marked by the historical and transcendent event of the Ascension.

This final stage stays closely linked to the first, that is, to his descent from heaven in the Incarnation. Only the one who "came from the Father" can return to the Father: Christ Jesus.<sup class="fn" data-fn="537">537</sup> "No one has ascended into heaven but he who descended from heaven, the Son of man."<sup class="fn" data-fn="538">538</sup> Left to its own natural powers humanity does not have access to the "Father's house", to God's life and happiness.<sup class="fn" data-fn="539">539</sup> Only Christ can open to man such access that we, his members, might have confidence that we too shall go where he, our Head and our Source, has preceded us.<sup class="fn" data-fn="540">540</sup>

"and I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all men to myself."<sup class="fn" data-fn="541">541</sup> The lifting up of Jesus on the cross signifies and announces his lifting up by his Ascension into heaven, and indeed begins it. Jesus Christ, the one priest of the new and eternal Covenant, "entered, not into a sanctuary made by human hands... but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf."<sup class="fn" data-fn="542">542</sup> There Christ permanently exercises his priesthood, for he "always lives to make intercession" for "those who draw near to God through him".<sup class="fn" data-fn="543">543</sup> As "high priest of the good things to come" he is the centre and the principal actor of the liturgy that honours the Father in heaven.<sup class="fn" data-fn="544">544</sup>

Henceforth Christ is seated at the right hand of the Father: "By 'the Father's right hand' we understand the glory and honour of divinity, where he who exists as Son of God before all ages, indeed as God, of one being with the Father, is seated bodily after he became incarnate and his flesh was glorified."<sup class="fn" data-fn="545">545</sup>

Being seated at the Father's right hand signifies the inauguration of the Messiah's kingdom, the fulfilment of the prophet Daniel's vision concerning the Son of man: "To him was given dominion and glory and kingdom, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him; his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom one that shall not be destroyed."<sup class="fn" data-fn="546">546</sup> After this event the apostles became witnesses of the "kingdom [that] will have no end".<sup class="fn" data-fn="547">547</sup>

Christ's Ascension marks the definitive entrance of Jesus' humanity into God's heavenly domain, whence he will come again (cf Acts 1:11); this humanity in the meantime hides him from the eyes of men (cf Col 3:3).
Jesus Christ, the head of the Church, precedes us into the Father's glorious kingdom so that we, the members of his Body, may live in the hope of one day being with him for ever.
Jesus Christ, having entered the sanctuary of heaven once and for all, intercedes constantly for us as the mediator who assures us of the permanent outpouring of the Holy Spirit.
Christ already reigns through the Church...
